messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into French, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE French line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
Je regardai en haut et vis ses épaules déjà vêtues des rayons de la planète qui mène les hommes droit sur chaque chemin.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table (Step 3)**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition (from Step 1) | Target Word / Phrase (French) | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|--------------------------------------|------------------------------|------------------------|--------| | guardai | “looked” – speaker’s upward gaze | regardai | looked | OK | | in | spatial preposition “on / in” | en | in/on | OK | | alto | “high” – direction of gaze | haut | high | OK | | e | coordinating “and” | et | and | OK | | vidi | “saw” – visual perception | vis | saw | OK | | le | definite article (fem. pl.) introducing “spalle” | — (omitted) | — | UNNECESSARY | | sue | possessive adjective “its” referring to the shoulders | ses | its | OK | | spalle | “shoulders” – object seen | épaules | shoulders | OK | | vestite | past participle “clothed” – state of shoulders | vêtues | clothed | OK | | già | adverb “already” – temporal marker | déjà | already | OK | | de' | preposition + article “of the” (introducing rays) | des | of the | OK | | raggi | “rays” – emanations of the planet | rayons | rays | OK | | del | preposition + article “of the” (linking planet) | de | of | OK | | pianeta | “planet” – source of rays | planète | planet | OK | | che | relative pronoun “that” (refers to planet) | qui | that | OK | | mena | verb “leadeth” – planet’s guiding action | mène | leads | OK | | dritto | adverb “aright / straight” – manner of leading | droit | straight | OK | | altrui | “men / people” – recipients of guidance | les hommes | men/people | OK | | per | preposition “along / for” – route of guidance | sur | on/along | OK | | ogne | determiner “every” – quantifier of paths | chaque | every | OK | | calle | “path” – route being guided | chemin | path | OK |
### Items Requiring Attention - **UNNECESSARY:** *le* – the Italian definite article is not expressed in French; the possessive *ses* already fulfills the function. - **MISSING / WRONG / GRAMMAR:** none.
All other source tokens are represented in the French translation with correct meaning, appropriate grammatical agreement, and no superfluous elements.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only French script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final French text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
